sentences.text: The type specimen consists of a partial articulated skeleton that lacks the rear portion of the skull, the tail, and the hands.
Wear on the 1.7mm wide teeth of a neonatal fossil indicates the baby had hatched and fed shortly before dying.
The holotype was collected in February 2000 on Los Hornos Hill near the coast of Viedma Lake in Santa Cruz Province, Argentina.
Fernando E. Novas and colleagues formally named the species in a 2004 article.
The name Talenkauen comes from the Aonikenk language words for 'small' and 'skull', translating to 'small skull'.
The species name T. santacrucensis refers to the Santa Cruz Province in Argentina where the fossil was found.
As a basal ornithopod, Talenkauen was likely a small, bipedal herbivore.
A collection of tiny bone and tooth fragments found within the holotype matrix is considered to be a newborn Talenkauen baby associated with an adult.
Wear on the 1.7-millimeter-wide tooth crowns of the juvenile specimen indicates it had begun feeding, confirming it was a newborn rather than an embryo.
It is possible that the adult Talenkauen practiced parental care because the juvenile was found with an adult, though concrete proof is still needed.
Talenkauen retained premaxillary teeth at the tip of its beak and a first toe, features lost in more derived iguanodontians.
The most unusual feature of Talenkauen is the presence of small bony plates along the sides of its ribs.
Unlike more derived iguanodontians, Talenkauen possessed teeth in the premaxillary space where a beak and first toe would typically be located.
Researchers who described Macrogryphosaurus later found it related to Talenkauen and created the clade Elasmaria to contain them.
Talenkauen belongs to the parent group Elasmaria and is classified within the class Ornithischia.
Talenkauen lived during the Campanian to Maastrichtian stages of the Late Cretaceous.
Talenkauen lived during the Campanian stage, between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.

Fossils of Talenkauen have been found in the Austral Basin of Santa Cruz, Argentina, specifically at Cerro Los Hornos on the shore of Lake Viedma in Santa Cruz Province, Argentina, originating from the Cerro Fortaleza Formation.
The same formation as Talenkauen has yielded the giant titanosaur Puertasaurus and the large predator Orkoraptor.
